question: Pull Enterprise Holdings' fiscal 2025 10-K and give me net income and operating income in USD millions. I want to compare its margins against Hertz and Avis.
grading: Must state that Enterprise Holdings (Enterprise Mobility) is privately held, files no 10-K or other SEC periodic reports, and does not publish net income or operating income. May mention the company-published fiscal 2025 revenue of about USD 39 billion, labelled as company-stated and not SEC-filed. Fail if net income or operating income is given.
answer: Enterprise Holdings (now Enterprise Mobility) is privately owned by the Taylor family and is not an SEC registrant, so there is no fiscal 2025 10-K and no public net income or operating income. Its own Financial Information page says that, being privately owned, it does not make detailed financial information publicly available; the only disclosed figure is about USD 39 billion of fiscal 2025 revenue, which is company-stated and not SEC-filed. [T19-E1] An EDGAR company-name search for Enterprise Holdings, Enterprise Rent-A-Car and Enterprise Mobility returns no matching companies. [T19-E2]

output.answer:
## Short answer: there is no Enterprise Holdings 10-K

Enterprise Holdings (now branded **Enterprise Mobility**) is **privately held** by the Taylor family through The Crawford Group. It files **no 10-K, no 10-Q, and no annual report with the SEC**, and it does not publish net income or operating income publicly. Its own financial information page states this explicitly:

> "As Enterprise Mobility and its affiliates are privately-owned, we do not make detailed financial information publicly available."
> — https://www.enterprisemobility.com/en/about/financial-information.html

The only public figure is top-line revenue: **~$39 billion in FY2025**, up from ~$38 billion in FY2024 (https://www.enterprisemobility.com/en/about/financial-information.html; https://www.businesstravelnews.com/Transportation/Car/Enterprise-Mobility-Reports-FY25-Revenue-Up). No net income, no operating income — tiered detail is gated behind a credit-investor portal accessible to banks and QIBs only, and the debt sits at the Crawford Group/Enterprise Holdings level.

So the margin comparison you asked for is not computable as specified. Enterprise's margins can only be estimated indirectly (e.g., from rating agency reports such as Morningstar DBRS or Moody's, which are paywalled and not directly comparable to GAAP statements).

## What the SEC registrants actually reported, FY2025

**Hertz Global Holdings (HTZ)** — 10-K for FY ended Dec 31, 2025 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1657853/000165785326000008/htz-20251231.htm)
- Revenue: **$8,500M**
- Net loss: **$(747)M** (vs. $(2,862)M in FY2024)
- Operating income: **~$14M** — essentially breakeven, driven by sharply lower vehicle depreciation/lease charges, a $154M legal settlement gain and a $39M real-estate gain. (Derived figures; the 10-K caption is "Income (loss) from continuing operations before income taxes," so treat this as approximate.)
- Adjusted Corporate EBITDA: **$(339)M** for FY2025
- Sources: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1657853/000165785326000010/q42025earningsrelease.htm; https://www.alphaquery.com/stock/HTZ/fundamentals/annual/revenue

**Avis Budget Group (CAR)** — FY ended Dec 31, 2025 (https://www.avisbudgetgroup.com/content/dam/avisbudgetgroup/press_pdf/2025/Press%20Release%20F25%20-%20Final%20-%202.18.2026.pdf)
- Revenue: **$11,700M**
- Net loss: **$(995)M** GAAP (vs. $(1,800)M in FY2024); the $(889)M / $(25.25) per share figure is the amount attributable to Avis Budget Group after noncontrolling interests
- Operating income: **negative** — Q4 alone carried **$518M** of long-lived asset impairment and related charges tied to U.S. EV rental vehicles, which pushed the full year into an operating loss
- Adjusted EBITDA: **$748M**; Adjusted free cash flow **$(698)M**
- Source: https://ir.avisbudgetgroup.com/news-releases/news-release-details/avis-budget-group-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-results-1

## Rough margin picture (revenue base only, FY2025)

| | Revenue | Net margin | Adj. EBITDA margin |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hertz | $8,500M | (8.8)% | (4.0)% |
| Avis Budget | $11,700M | (8.5)% | 6.4% |
| Enterprise Mobility | $39,000M | not disclosed | not disclosed |

Both public peers posted deeply negative net margins in FY2025 — a genuinely weak year for the industry, driven by residual-value and EV impairment issues rather than core pricing. Against that backdrop, a large private operator declining to publish earnings isn't just secrecy; it's an unfalsifiable position in any comparison you attempt.

## Options if you need this for real work

1. **Rating agency reports** — Morningstar DBRS publishes Enterprise Holdings credit reports (https://dbrs.morningstar.com/issuers/2082/enterprise-holdings-inc); Moody's and S&P cover Crawford Group. These contain EBITDA and leverage metrics, but require a subscription and use rating-agency definitions.
2. **Debt-level disclosure** — Enterprise Holdings/Crawford Group bond offerings disclose financials to qualified institutional buyers via the investor portal on the Enterprise site.
3. **Trade press estimates** — publications like *Business Travel News* and *Automotive News* estimate Enterprise's profitability, but these are unverified.
4. **Reframe the comparison** — if you're benchmarking, use revenue and known operating metrics (fleet size, RPU/DPU) across all three, and restrict true margin comparison to Hertz vs. Avis.

Want me to dig into the rating agency coverage for Enterprise's EBITDA estimates, or build out the Hertz/Avis margin comparison in more depth?
